```{r QCbarplot, results='asis'}

###### generated in ccrvb47_LIONscRNAseq_batch123_38samps_QCBatchCorrectionSubclustering_KCG.Rmd QC_summary chunk

stats_df <- readRDS(file = file.path(outputRData_dir,"ccrvb47_batch123_38samps_QC_stats_df.rds"))



####### stacked barplot

    cat("### ",paste0( "Filtered proportions "),"\n")
cat("\n")

stats_df2 <- stats_df %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c("sample",colnames(.)[startsWith(colnames(.),"Num_")]))) %>%
    ## make longer
    tidyr::pivot_longer(!sample, names_to = "Filtering", values_to = "NumCells") %>%
    ## simplify names
    dplyr::mutate(Filtering = str_remove_all(Filtering,"Num_"),
                  Tissue = factor(ifelse(grepl("PBMC",as.character(sample)),"PBMC","LN"),c("PBMC","LN")),
                  TimePoint = factor(str_after_last(as.character(sample),"_"), c("PRE","DAY2","DAY8")),
                  MacaqueID = factor(str_before_first(as.character(sample),"_"), c("MB59","MC73","MC90","MC98","MF07","MF30"))
                  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Tissue, TimePoint, MacaqueID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(sample = factor(sample, unique(sample))) 

p <- stats_df2 %>%
  ggplot(aes(y=NumCells, x=sample, fill=Filtering, label = NumCells
             ))+
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Doublets="#FFC1FF",MiQCdiscard="#FEFA7F",Retained ="#B3FFCE"))+  
    geom_bar(stat="identity",position = "fill")+
  ylab("Pct")+
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = NumCells),
    #label = ifelse(batch == "PBMC2", NumCells,"")),
           position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5), 
    #nudge_x = 0.5, 
    vjust = 1, hjust = 0.5, 
    size =3, min.segment.length = 1, 
    direction = "x"
            )+
  
  
    theme_bw()+
  #### rotate x axis labels
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))

plot(p)
  cat("\n")
cat(' \n \n') ### this is the key!


#### save to lists
list_of_plotted[[paste0(fig_name_to_use)]] <- stats_df2
```

```{r addFINALNAMES, eval=TRUE}

############ replace this with using the ccrvb47_FINALNAMESonly.xlsx
finalnames_df <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(file.path(parent_dir, "input_data", "ccrvb47_FINALNAMESonly.xlsx")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  dplyr::rename(final_name = final_name_051926) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(original_name, final_name), trimws))

## sanity check: flag any clusters that didn't find a match in the Excel file
current_clusters <- unique(as.character(seuratObj_to_use$respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs))
unmatched <- dplyr::setdiff(current_clusters, finalnames_df$original_name)
if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
  warning("The following original names had no match in ccrvb47_FINALNAMESonly.xlsx: ",
          paste(unmatched, collapse = ", "))
}

## map old cluster labels to final names via left_join
seuratObj_to_use$respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs_FINALname <- 
  tibble::tibble(original_name = as.character(seuratObj_to_use$respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(finalnames_df %>% dplyr::select(original_name, final_name),
                    by = "original_name") %>%
  dplyr::pull(final_name)

#### factorize using the excel-defined order (reversed so myeloid is on top of dotplots)
level_order <- finalnames_df %>%
  dplyr::arrange(final_order) %>%
  dplyr::pull(final_name) #%>%
 # rev() ### do not reverse to get the colors correct

seuratObj_to_use$respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs_FINALname <- factor(
  seuratObj_to_use$respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs_FINALname,
  levels = level_order
)




res_to_use <- "respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs_FINALname"

comp_df <- seuratObj_to_use@meta.data[, c("respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs", res_to_use)] %>%
  unique() %>%
  ### rename to generic
  dplyr::rename(respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs=1,res_col=2) %>%
  ## factorize
  dplyr::mutate(respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs = factor(respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs, levels(seuratObj_to_use$respt4_rpca_ClustersWithSubs)),
                res_col = factor(res_col, levels = levels(seuratObj_to_use[[res_to_use]][, res_to_use]))) 



```

## `r paste0(fig_name_to_use," : ",long_name_to_use)` {.tabset}

TISSUE TRIMMED = subclusters/clusters were removed if < 3 cells in at least 7/15 LN or 11/22 PBMC samples

### Butterfly (ignoring time) {.tabset}

``` {r butterfly_group1, fig.height=10, fig.width = 10, results = 'asis'}
### set levels
### for res that already have levels
if(grepl(paste(c("SLM_", "Clusters","clusters","BROAD"),collapse = '|'),res_to_use)){
  clust_levels <- levels(seuratObj_to_use[[res_to_use]][,res_to_use])
}else{
  clust_levels <- make.names(c(sort(unique(seuratObj_to_use[[res_to_use]][,res_to_use])),"NA"))
}



  
 group_tab <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(seuratObj_to_use[[c(res_to_use,"Tissue")]], useNA = "ifany")) %>%
  rownames_to_column("cluster") %>%

  ### collect % of each celltype 
  
  ### make longer 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = !cluster, names_to = "Tissue", values_to = "NumCells") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Tissue) %>%
  ### collect % of each sample (i.e Tissue)
  group_by(Tissue) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pct = round(100*NumCells/sum(NumCells),4)) %>%
  ungroup() 


breaks_to_use <- seq(-15, 15, by = 1)

v <- group_tab %>%
  dplyr::select(cluster, Tissue,pct, NumCells) %>%
  ## make PBMC negative since on left
  dplyr::mutate(pct = ifelse(Tissue == "PBMC", (-1)*pct, pct),
                cluster = factor(cluster, rev(clust_levels))) %>% ### so puts first on top
  dplyr::arrange(cluster) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = cluster, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_col() +
    geom_text(aes(label = NumCells,
                x     = ifelse(Tissue == "PBMC", pct - 1, pct + 1),
                hjust = ifelse(Tissue == "PBMC", 1, 0)),
            size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey30") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = breaks_to_use,
    labels = abs(breaks_to_use),
    limits = c(min(breaks_to_use), max(breaks_to_use))    # adjust to your data range
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rev(cols_to_use)) +
  labs(
    x    = "% of Total cells per tissue",
    y    = "Cluster",
    fill = "Cluster"
  ) +
```

```{r DotplotToList_clusterOnly}

######### save plotted data (ignoring time/tissue) - ONLY HAVE TO GENERATE THIS ONCE
#### ordered factor to be able to add lines
seuratObj_to_use[[res_to_use]][,res_to_use] <- ordered(seuratObj_to_use[[res_to_use]][,res_to_use], levels=levels(seuratObj_to_use[[res_to_use]][,res_to_use]))
################### definte Pct summary function, assumes threshold = 0
Pct_summary <- function(x){
  return(sum(x > 0) / length(x) * 100)
}


#################### separates by tissue only
####### process seurat object to be smaller dataframe - only has to be done once, doesn't run with the app
##### needs to be run on biowulf since needs a lot of memory to do the summary step
# https://github.com/dpcook/code_snippets/blob/main/20210510_recreate_seurat_dotplot/recreate_seurat_dotplot.md
### get expression data
exp_mat <- as.matrix(seuratObj_to_use[["SCT"]]@data)
### get cluster assignments

########## columns are cluster/tissue, (Gene), Avg, Pct; rows are genes
meta_summary <- seuratObj_to_use@meta.data %>% 
  dplyr::select(!!rlang::sym(res_to_use)) %>%
  ### add generic cluster 
  dplyr::mutate(cluster = paste0(!!rlang::sym(res_to_use))) %>%
  dplyr::select(-!!rlang::sym(res_to_use)) %>%
  ### add in transposed expression
  bind_cols(as.data.frame(t(exp_mat))) %>%
  ####columns are cluster/tissue & genes, rows are cell names
  
  ### cannot make long format now since too many rows for cells x genes x groups
  #### instead group by cluster_Tissue
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  ### gives df with rows = cluster_tissue group and columns = gene_mean, gene_Pct
  dplyr::summarise(across(everything(), list(Avg = mean, Pct = Pct_summary))) %>%
  ### now can make longer
  pivot_longer(-cluster, names_to="Gene_stat", values_to="value") %>%
  ### separate gene_stat
  dplyr::mutate(Gene = str_before_last(Gene_stat,"_"),
                stat = str_after_last(Gene_stat,"_"),
                Gene_stat = NULL) %>%
  ### make wider
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "stat", values_from = "value")


 ####### save to plotted
```

```{r TIMEdegHM_prep, results='asis', fig.height=12}
consTimeMarkers_df <- readRDS(file.path(outputRData_dir,paste0(marker_list_name_to_use,
                                                             "_FindConservedTimeMarkers_DF_",
                                                             test_to_use,"_",assay_to_use,
                                                             "_minpct",str_replace(minpct_to_use,"\\.","pt"),
                                                             "_logfc",str_replace(logfc_to_use,"\\.","pt"),
                                                             "_",subset_res_to_use,".rds"))) %>%
  ### NOTE: recode cluster names using xlsx-derived name_map (original -> final name)
  ### cluster values here are of form "<clustername>_<PBMC/LN><up/dn>", so recode
  ### only the portion before the first underscore, leaving the tissue/dir suffix intact
  dplyr::mutate(
    cluster = paste0(
      dplyr::recode(str_before_first(cluster, "_"), !!!name_map),
      "_",
      str_after_first(cluster, "_")
    )
  ) %>%
  ### NOTE: drop rows for any cluster not present in finalnames_df (i.e.
  ### trimmed), so consTimeMarkers_df itself only ever contains the retained
  ### cluster set -- protects any future chunk that reads this df directly
  ### without its own explicit filter/loop-over-colors_df scoping
  dplyr::filter(str_before_first(cluster, "_") %in% new_cluster_order)





### NOTE: ct_cat_list is built from finalnames_df$broad_category rather than
### hardcoded substring patterns, so it stays correct regardless of what the
### final cluster name strings look like. This assumes curr_ct at the point
### ct_cat_list is used has already been recoded to final names (see Edit 5) --
### if not yet recoded, this dictionary would need to key on original_name instead.
ct_cat_list <- split(finalnames_df$final_name_051926, finalnames_df$broad_category)

### "MyeNeut" and "NeutOnly" aren't broad_category values in the xlsx (the xlsx
### only has "Myeloid" and "Neutrophil" as separate categories) but the original
### code needs combined/renamed variants, so build those explicitly:
ct_cat_list[["MyeNeut"]] <- c(ct_cat_list[["Myeloid"]], ct_cat_list[["Neutrophil"]])
ct_cat_list[["MyeOnly"]] <- ct_cat_list[["Myeloid"]]
ct_cat_list[["NeutOnly"]] <- ct_cat_list[["Neutrophil"]]
### "NK" category name in xlsx broad_category matches original list's "NK" key already
### "otherT" and "Bcell"/"CD4"/"CD8" keys also already match broad_category values,
### assuming the xlsx used those exact capitalizations (check finalnames_df$broad_category
### unique values match: Bcell, CD4, CD8, otherT, NK, Myeloid, Neutrophil, Platelet,
### Prog, Erythro, GATA3, otherContam)
```

```{r reformatAndEnrichments, results='asis', fig.height=12, eval=eval_reformatAndEnrichments}
            grepl("dn", which_animals_sig) & !grepl("up", which_animals_sig) ~ "down",
            
            # --- Both up and dn present ---
            num_animals_sig <= 4 ~ "up_down",                     # too few significant animals
            num_animals_sig > 4 & num_dn == 1 ~ "up",             # one dn among many up
            num_animals_sig > 4 & num_up == 1 ~ "down",           # one up among many dn
            num_animals_sig > 4 & num_up > 1 & num_dn > 1 ~ "up_down",  # mixed signals
            
            # --- Otherwise ---

            MB59_p_val_adj = ifelse(MB59_sig == "_",

            MF30_p_val_adj = ifelse(MF30_sig == "_",

          ) %>%

          dplyr::select(gene, cluster, contrast, colnames(.)[grepl(paste(c("_avg_log2FC","_p_val_adj"), collapse = '|'), colnames(.))]) %>%
          ### add mean of each
          rowwise() %>%

                        meanAcrossAnimals_pval_adj = mean(c_across(ends_with("_p_val_adj")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
          ungroup() %>%
          ## move these to the front
          dplyr::relocate(c(meanAcrossAnimals_log2FC,meanAcrossAnimals_pval_adj),.after = "contrast")
        
        ######### save to list
```

```{r summaryplots, results='asis', fig.width = 12}
plotted_values_df <- data.frame()
clust_per_gene_collected_df <- data.frame()

###### for each tissue separately


### =========================================================================
### STEP 1: Add this BEFORE the `for(curr_tiss in c("LN","PBMC"))` loop
### (i.e. right before the summaryplots chunk's main tissue loop starts).
### This does a lightweight pre-pass to compute, per curr_contrast, the max
### |value| across BOTH tissues, so the butterfly plot's y-axis (which
### becomes the x-axis after coord_flip()) can be shared within a contrast
### but still differ freely across the three contrasts.
### =========================================================================

## ---- PRE-PASS: compute shared y-limits per contrast, across both tissues ----

contrast_axis_limits <- list()

for(precomp_contrast in c("DAY2vsPREonly","DAY2andDAY8vsPRE","DAY8vsPREonly")){

  max_val_this_contrast <- 0

  for(precomp_tiss in c("LN","PBMC")){

    if(precomp_tiss == "PBMC"){
      more_than_x_animals_pc <- 3
    }

    if(grepl("and", precomp_contrast)){
      contrasts_to_use_pc <- c("DAY2vsPRE","DAY8vsPRE")
    }else{
      contrasts_to_use_pc <- str_remove_all(precomp_contrast,"only")
    }

    curr_df2_pc <- consTimeMarkers_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(Tissue == precomp_tiss) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(tiss_dir = str_after_first(cluster, "_"),
                    cluster = str_before_first(cluster,"_"),
                    dir_contrast = str_remove_all(str_remove_all(tiss_dir,"PBMC"),"LN"),
                    dir = ifelse(grepl("up",dir_contrast),"up","down"),
                    contrast = str_remove_all(str_remove_all(dir_contrast,"up"),"dn")) %>%
      dplyr::filter(cluster %in% new_cluster_order) %>%
      dplyr::filter(contrast != "DAY8vsDAY2") %>%
      dplyr::filter(avg_log2FC > log2FC_cut | avg_log2FC < -log2FC_cut) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        MB59_sig = ifelse(MB59_p_val_adj < 0.05, ifelse(MB59_avg_log2FC > 0, "upMB59", "dnMB59"), "_"),
        MC90_sig = ifelse(MC90_p_val_adj < 0.05, ifelse(MC90_avg_log2FC > 0, "upMC90", "dnMC90"), "_"),
        MC98_sig = ifelse(MC98_p_val_adj < 0.05, ifelse(MC98_avg_log2FC > 0, "upMC98", "dnMC98"), "_"),
        MC73_sig = ifelse(MC73_p_val_adj < 0.05, ifelse(MC73_avg_log2FC > 0, "upMC73", "dnMC73"), "_"),
        MF07_sig = ifelse(MF07_p_val_adj < 0.05, ifelse(MF07_avg_log2FC > 0, "upMF07", "dnMF07"), "_"),
        MF30_sig = ifelse(MF30_p_val_adj < 0.05, ifelse(MF30_avg_log2FC > 0, "upMF30", "dnMF30"), "_"),
        which_animals_sig = paste0(MB59_sig,MC90_sig,MC98_sig,MC73_sig,MF07_sig,MF30_sig),
        which_animals_sig_LNfilter = paste0(MB59_sig,MC90_sig,MC98_sig),
        num_animals_sig = 6-str_count(which_animals_sig,"_"),
        num_up = str_count(which_animals_sig, "up"),
        num_dn = str_count(which_animals_sig, "dn"),
        dir_combo = case_when(
          grepl("up", which_animals_sig) & !grepl("dn", which_animals_sig) ~ "up",
          grepl("dn", which_animals_sig) & !grepl("up", which_animals_sig) ~ "down",
          num_animals_sig <= 4 ~ "up_down",
          num_animals_sig > 4 & num_dn == 1 ~ "up",
          num_animals_sig > 4 & num_up == 1 ~ "down",
          num_animals_sig > 4 & num_up > 1 & num_dn > 1 ~ "up_down",
          TRUE ~ "not_sig"
        ),
        cluster_dir = paste0(cluster,"__",dir_combo)) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!dir_combo %in% c("not_sig","up_down")) %>%
      dplyr::filter(!grepl("ENSMMUG00",gene)) %>%
      {
        if(precomp_tiss == "LN"){
          dplyr::filter(.,
            (grepl("upMB59", which_animals_sig_LNfilter) &
             grepl("upMC90", which_animals_sig_LNfilter) &
             grepl("upMC98", which_animals_sig_LNfilter)) |
            (grepl("dnMB59", which_animals_sig_LNfilter) &
             grepl("dnMC90", which_animals_sig_LNfilter) &
             grepl("dnMC98", which_animals_sig_LNfilter))
          )
        }else{
          dplyr::filter(., str_count(which_animals_sig,"M") > more_than_x_animals_pc)
        }
      } %>%
      dplyr::arrange(contrast) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(gene, cluster) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        has_DAY2 = any(grepl("DAY2vsPRE", dir_contrast, fixed = TRUE)),
        has_DAY8 = any(grepl("DAY8vsPRE", dir_contrast, fixed = TRUE)),
        dir_DAY2DAY8 = paste(unique(dir),collapse = '_')
      ) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        ( all(c("DAY2vsPRE", "DAY8vsPRE") %in% contrasts_to_use_pc) & has_DAY2 & has_DAY8 ) |
        ( length(contrasts_to_use_pc) == 1 && contrasts_to_use_pc == "DAY2vsPRE" & has_DAY2 & !has_DAY8 ) |
        ( length(contrasts_to_use_pc) == 1 && contrasts_to_use_pc == "DAY8vsPRE" & has_DAY8 & !has_DAY2 )
      ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(cluster_gene = paste0(cluster,"____",gene)) %>%
      dplyr::filter(contrast == contrasts_to_use_pc[1])

    if(nrow(curr_df2_pc) == 0) next

    clusters_order_pc <- colors_df$cluster

    na_list_unique_pc <- list(up_TOTAL=0,dn_TOTAL=0,up_UNIQUE=0,dn_UNIQUE=0)
    new_names_pc <- paste0(str_before_first(names(na_list_unique_pc),"_"),precomp_contrast,"_",str_after_first(names(na_list_unique_pc),"_"))
    names(na_list_unique_pc) <- new_names_pc

    ### genes appearing in exactly 1 DISTINCT cluster (for this tissue/contrast)
    ### -- must count distinct clusters per gene (matching how Num_clusters /
    ### clust_per_gene is derived in the main loop), NOT just row counts. A
    ### gene can have >1 row for the same cluster (e.g. duplicate entries),
    ### so table(gene) alone would undercount true multi-row-but-1-cluster
    ### genes as "not unique" and incorrectly drop them from the UNIQUE tally,
    ### which is what was chopping values.
    genes_in_one_cluster_pc <- curr_df2_pc %>%
      dplyr::distinct(gene, cluster) %>%
      dplyr::count(gene, name = "Num_clusters") %>%
      dplyr::filter(Num_clusters == 1) %>%
      dplyr::pull(gene) %>%
      as.character()

    curr_df2_pc_unique_only <- curr_df2_pc %>%
      dplyr::filter(gene %in% genes_in_one_cluster_pc)

    unique_df_pc <- as.data.frame(table(curr_df2_pc_unique_only$cluster_dir)) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(cluster = factor(str_before_first(as.character(Var1),"__"),clusters_order_pc),
                    dir = factor(paste0(str_replace_all(str_after_first(as.character(Var1),"__"),"down","dn"),
                                        precomp_contrast,"_UNIQUE"),c(paste0("up",precomp_contrast,"_UNIQUE"),
                                                                      paste0("dn",precomp_contrast,"_UNIQUE"))),
                    Var1 = NULL) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(cluster, dir) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "dir", values_from = "Freq")

    total_unique_df_pc <- as.data.frame(table(curr_df2_pc$cluster_dir)) %>%
      dplyr::rename(cluster=Var1,Num_DEGs=Freq) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(cluster) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(cluster_dir=paste0(cluster),
                    cluster = factor(str_before_first(cluster_dir,"__"),clusters_order_pc),
                    dir = factor(paste0(str_replace_all(str_after_first(as.character(cluster_dir),"__"),"down","dn"),
                                        precomp_contrast,"_TOTAL"),c(paste0("up",precomp_contrast,"_TOTAL"),
                                                                      paste0("dn",precomp_contrast,"_TOTAL"))),
                    cluster_dir=NULL) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(cluster, dir) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "dir", values_from = "Num_DEGs") %>%
      dplyr::left_join(unique_df_pc, by = "cluster") %>%
      replace_na(na_list_unique_pc)

    prep_butterfly_pc <- total_unique_df_pc %>%
      dplyr::mutate(up_SHARED = !!rlang::sym(new_names_pc[1])-!!rlang::sym(new_names_pc[3]),
                    dn_SHARED = !!rlang::sym(new_names_pc[2])-!!rlang::sym(new_names_pc[4])) %>%
      dplyr::select(-ends_with("TOTAL")) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(!cluster, names_to = "dir_cat", values_to = "value") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(value = ifelse(grepl("^dn", dir_cat), -1*value, value))

    ### IMPORTANT: geom_bar(stat="identity") STACKS same-signed dir_cat values
    ### within each cluster, so the true rendered bar extent per cluster is the
    ### SUM of its positive-side values and the SUM (abs) of its negative-side
    ### values -- NOT the single largest individual value. Taking
    ### max(abs(value)) undercounts any cluster where UNIQUE + SHARED on the
    ### same side both contribute (e.g. CL mono F4's dn_UNIQUE + dn_SHARED
    ### stack exceeding either value alone), which is what caused clipping.
    stack_extents_pc <- prep_butterfly_pc %>%
      dplyr::group_by(cluster) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(
        pos_stack = sum(value[value > 0], na.rm = TRUE),
        neg_stack = sum(abs(value[value < 0]), na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )

    max_stack_pc <- max(c(stack_extents_pc$pos_stack, stack_extents_pc$neg_stack), na.rm = TRUE)

    max_val_this_contrast <- max(max_val_this_contrast, max_stack_pc)
  }

  ### add a little headroom (5%) so bars don't touch the panel edge
  contrast_axis_limits[[precomp_contrast]] <- max_val_this_contrast * 1.05
}

## ---- END PRE-PASS ----

for(curr_tiss in c("LN","PBMC")){

      ### remove not_sig & mixed signals

      unite("up_down", up_total:down_total, na.rm=TRUE) %>% ### is the gene up or down or both across clusters
```

```{r Ifn_prep, results='asis', fig.height=12}
consTimeMarkers_df <- readRDS(file.path(outputRData_dir,paste0(marker_list_name_to_use,
                                                             "_FindConservedTimeMarkers_DF_",
                                                             test_to_use,"_",assay_to_use,
                                                             "_minpct",str_replace(minpct_to_use,"\\.","pt"),
                                                             "_logfc",str_replace(logfc_to_use,"\\.","pt"),
                                                             "_",subset_res_to_use,".rds"))) %>%
  ### NOTE: recode cluster names using xlsx-derived name_map (original -> final
  ### name) right here, at the earliest possible point, so that `cluster` is
  ### the FINAL name for every single row from this point forward in the
  ### entire document. consTimeMarkers_df's cluster values are of form
  ### "<clustername>_<PBMC/LN><up/dn>", so recode only the portion before the
  ### first underscore, leaving the tissue/dir suffix intact.
  dplyr::mutate(
    cluster = paste0(
      dplyr::recode(str_before_first(cluster, "_"), !!!name_map),
      "_",
      str_after_first(cluster, "_")
    )
  ) %>%
  ### NOTE: drop rows for any cluster not present in finalnames_df (i.e.
  ### trimmed) -- this is the single point that guarantees a trimmed cluster
  ### can never reach any downstream figure/table/network, regardless of
  ### whether an individual figure-specific chunk later in the document
  ### remembers to filter or join to finalnames_df itself.
  dplyr::filter(str_before_first(cluster, "_") %in% new_cluster_order)




    
    curr_degs_df_trim <- consTimeMarkers_df %>%
      ### separate dir from cluster name
      dplyr::mutate(tiss_dir = str_after_first(cluster, "_"),
                    cluster = str_before_first(cluster,"_"),
                    dir_contrast = str_remove_all(str_remove_all(tiss_dir,"PBMC"),"LN"),
                    dir = ifelse(grepl("up",dir_contrast),"up","down"),
                    contrast = str_remove_all(str_remove_all(dir_contrast,"up"),"dn")) %>%
      
      
      ## also trim to big avg_log2FC (this is before removing non-sig diff log2FC animals)
      dplyr::filter(avg_log2FC > log2FC_cut | avg_log2FC < -log2FC_cut) %>%

      #### add  which animals sig
      dplyr::mutate(
        MB59_sig = ifelse(MB59_p_val_adj < 0.05,
                          ifelse(MB59_avg_log2FC > 0,
                                 "upMB59",
                                 "dnMB59"),
                          "_"),
        MC90_sig = ifelse(MC90_p_val_adj < 0.05,
                          ifelse(MC90_avg_log2FC > 0,
                                 "upMC90",
                                 "dnMC90"),
                          "_"),
        MC98_sig = ifelse(MC98_p_val_adj < 0.05,
                          ifelse(MC98_avg_log2FC > 0,
                                 "upMC98",
                                 "dnMC98"),
                          "_"),
        MC73_sig = ifelse(MC73_p_val_adj < 0.05,
                          ifelse(MC73_avg_log2FC > 0,
                                 "upMC73",
                                 "dnMC73"),
                          "_"),
        MF07_sig = ifelse(MF07_p_val_adj < 0.05,
                          ifelse(MF07_avg_log2FC > 0,
                                 "upMF07",
                                 "dnMF07"),
                          "_"),
        MF30_sig = ifelse(MF30_p_val_adj < 0.05,
                          ifelse(MF30_avg_log2FC > 0,
                                 "upMF30",
                                 "dnMF30"),
                          "_"),
      
      ### set avg_log2FC & p_adj to NA if not sig
          MB59_avg_log2FC = ifelse(MB59_sig == "_",
                                   NA,
                                   MB59_avg_log2FC),
          MC90_avg_log2FC = ifelse(MC90_sig == "_",
                                   NA,
                                   MC90_avg_log2FC),
          MC98_avg_log2FC = ifelse(MC98_sig == "_",
                                   NA,
                                   MC98_avg_log2FC),
          MC73_avg_log2FC = ifelse(MC73_sig == "_",
                                   NA,
                                   MC73_avg_log2FC),
          MF07_avg_log2FC = ifelse(MF07_sig == "_",
                                   NA,
                                   MF07_avg_log2FC),
          MF30_avg_log2FC = ifelse(MF30_sig == "_",
                                   NA,
                                   MF30_avg_log2FC),
          MB59_p_val_adj = ifelse(MB59_sig == "_",
                                  NA,
                                  MB59_p_val_adj),
          MC90_p_val_adj = ifelse(MC90_sig == "_",
                                  NA,
                                  MC90_p_val_adj),
          MC98_p_val_adj = ifelse(MC98_sig == "_",
                                  NA,
                                  MC98_p_val_adj),
          MC73_p_val_adj = ifelse(MC73_sig == "_",
                                  NA,
                                  MC73_p_val_adj),
          MF07_p_val_adj = ifelse(MF07_sig == "_",
                                  NA,
                                  MF07_p_val_adj),
          MF30_p_val_adj = ifelse(MF30_sig == "_",
                                  NA,
                                  MF30_p_val_adj)
          
        ) %>%
        
        ### add mean of each
        rowwise() %>%
        dplyr::mutate(meanAcrossAnimals_log2FC = mean(c_across(ends_with("_avg_log2FC")), na.rm = TRUE),
                      meanAcrossAnimals_pval_adj = mean(c_across(ends_with("_p_val_adj")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
      
      
      dplyr::mutate(
        
        which_animals_sig = paste0(MB59_sig,MC90_sig,MC98_sig,MC73_sig,MF07_sig,MF30_sig),
        num_animals_sig = 6-str_count(which_animals_sig,"_"),
        which_animals_sig_LNfilter = paste0(MB59_sig,MC90_sig,MC98_sig),
        num_up = str_count(which_animals_sig, "up"),
        num_dn = str_count(which_animals_sig, "dn"),
        dir_combo = case_when(
          # --- Only one direction present ---
          grepl("up", which_animals_sig) & !grepl("dn", which_animals_sig) ~ "up",
          grepl("dn", which_animals_sig) & !grepl("up", which_animals_sig) ~ "down",
          
          # --- Both up and dn present ---
          num_animals_sig <= 4 ~ "up_down",                     # too few significant animals
          num_animals_sig > 4 & num_dn == 1 ~ "up",             # one dn among many up
          num_animals_sig > 4 & num_up == 1 ~ "down",           # one up among many dn
          num_animals_sig > 4 & num_up > 1 & num_dn > 1 ~ "up_down",  # mixed signals
          
          # --- Otherwise ---
          TRUE ~ "not_sig"
        )) %>%
      ### remove not_sig & mixed signals
      dplyr::filter(!dir_combo %in% c("not_sig","up_down")) %>%
      ### also remove unknown genes
      dplyr::filter(!grepl("ENSMMUG00",gene)) %>%
      #### at least 2  (LN) or 4 (PBMC) animals are sig
     # dplyr::mutate(more_than_x_animals = ifelse(Tissue == "PBMC", 3, 1)) %>%
     # dplyr::filter(str_count(which_animals_sig,"M") > more_than_x_animals) 
      #### all3LN animals or at least 4 PBMC
      dplyr::mutate(more_than_x_animals = ifelse(Tissue == "PBMC", 3, NA)) %>%
dplyr::filter(
  (Tissue == "PBMC" & str_count(which_animals_sig,"M") > more_than_x_animals) |
  (Tissue == "LN" & 
     ((grepl("upMB59", which_animals_sig_LNfilter) & 
       grepl("upMC90", which_animals_sig_LNfilter) & 
       grepl("upMC98", which_animals_sig_LNfilter)) |
      (grepl("dnMB59", which_animals_sig_LNfilter) & 
       grepl("dnMC90", which_animals_sig_LNfilter) & 
       grepl("dnMC98", which_animals_sig_LNfilter)))
  )
)

### NOTE: list_of_enrichments keys are of form "<cluster>_<tissue>_<dir><contrast>",
### e.g. "CD8 DP gd l24_PBMC_upvsPRE" -- these keys were written under OLD
### cluster names by the summary Rmd (whether or not that Rmd's own naming
### work has been re-run there). Recode just the cluster portion of each key
### to the final name here, once, so every downstream reference in this
### document (names_df, list_of_broadCats matching, network/volcano chunks)
### operates on final names consistently with curr_degs_df_trim above.
### dplyr::recode() passes through unmatched (i.e. trimmed) names unchanged,
### so we additionally drop any key whose cluster portion isn't in
### new_cluster_order, keeping list_of_enrichments trimmed to the same
### retained cluster set as curr_degs_df_trim.
names(list_of_enrichments) <- paste0(
  dplyr::recode(str_before_first(names(list_of_enrichments), "_"), !!!name_map),
  "_",
  str_after_first(names(list_of_enrichments), "_")
)

]

names_df <- data.frame("cluster_tiss_dir"=names(list_of_enrichments)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cluster = str_before_first(cluster_tiss_dir,"_"),
                tissue_dir = str_after_first(cluster_tiss_dir,"_"),

                                      paste0(str_before_first(dir,"_"),"DAY2vsPRE_",

                                                    ### NOTE: these cluster_tiss_dir literals were written against OLD

                                                    ### built from final names (Step 4/5 above), translate the cluster

                                                    ifelse(cluster_tiss_dir %in% c(paste0(unname(name_map["CD8 DP gd l24"]),"_PBMC_upvsPRE")), ### was "CD8 DP gd l24_PBMC_upvsPRE"
                                                           paste0("notSigDAY2vsPRE_",str_remove_all(dir,"vsPRE"),"DAY8vsPRE"),

                                                                  paste0(str_remove_all(dir,"vsPRE"),"DAY2vsPRE_notSigDAY8vsPRE"),
                                                                  "NOT"))),

                                                    "NOT"))),

                simp_dir = str_remove_all(str_remove_all(str_remove_all(complete_dir,"DAY2vsPRE"),"DAY8vsPRE"),"DAY8vsDAY2"),
                interpretation = ifelse(simp_dir == "up_up_up",
                                        "up at DAY2, increases more at DAY8",
```

```{r network, results='asis', fig.height=15, fig.width=20}
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Map original Terms -> collapsed Terms

# Apply mapping back to df

  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-combined_term)

}else{
  
  ##### otherwise collapse by 80% similarity

# Collapse Terms that share at least 80% of genes
term_gene_sets <- df_net %>%
  dplyr::distinct(.data[[term_col]], .data[[gene_col]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data[[term_col]]) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    genes = list(sort(unique(.data[[gene_col]]))),
    n_genes = length(unique(.data[[gene_col]])),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Pairwise overlap coefficient between terms
term_pairs <- utils::combn(term_gene_sets[[term_col]], 2, simplify = FALSE)

pair_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(term_pairs, function(pair) {
  t1 <- pair[1]
  t2 <- pair[2]

  g1 <- term_gene_sets$genes[[match(t1, term_gene_sets[[term_col]])]]
  g2 <- term_gene_sets$genes[[match(t2, term_gene_sets[[term_col]])]]

  shared <- length(intersect(g1, g2))
  denom <- min(length(g1), length(g2))
  overlap <- if (denom == 0) 0 else shared / denom

  dplyr::tibble(
    term1 = t1,
    term2 = t2,
    overlap = overlap
  )
})) %>%
  dplyr::filter(overlap >= 0.8)

# Build connected components of highly-overlapping terms
if (nrow(pair_df) > 0) {
  term_graph <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
    pair_df %>% dplyr::select(term1, term2),
    directed = FALSE,
    vertices = term_gene_sets %>% dplyr::select(name = .data[[term_col]])
  )

  comp <- igraph::components(term_graph)

  term_clusters <- tibble::tibble(
    original_term = names(comp$membership),
    cluster_id = unname(comp$membership)
  )
} else {
  term_clusters <- term_gene_sets %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      original_term = .data[[term_col]],
      cluster_id = dplyr::row_number()
    )
}

# Create combined term labels
collapsed_terms <- term_clusters %>%
  dplyr::group_by(cluster_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    combined_term = if (dplyr::n() > 1) {
      paste0("COMBINED_", dplyr::first(original_term))
    } else {
      dplyr::first(original_term)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )

term_map <- term_clusters %>%
  dplyr::left_join(collapsed_terms, by = "cluster_id") %>%
  dplyr::select(original_term, combined_term)




#### save to plotted

nodes <- nodes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    term = dplyr::if_else(type == "Term", label, NA_character_),
    term_col = term_pal[term]
  )

  g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(edges, directed = FALSE, vertices = nodes)

# Force-directed 2D layout instead of bipartite layout
set.seed(1)
lay <- igraph::layout_with_fr(
  g,
  niter = niter_to_use,
 # start.temp = sqrt(igraph::vcount(g)) * 2,
  #grid = "nogrid"
)


#lay <- igraph::layout_with_drl(g)

# Convert layout to polar coordinates
theta <- atan2(lay[,2], lay[,1])
rho   <- sqrt(lay[,1]^2 + lay[,2]^2)

# Identify node types in same order as layout
node_type <- nodes$type[match(igraph::V(g)$name, nodes$name)]

# Rescale radius separately:
# Genes = inner circle, Terms = outer ring
rho_scaled <- ifelse(
  node_type == "Gene",
  scales::rescale(rho, to = c(0.0, 1.0)),   # inner region
  scales::rescale(rho, to = c(1.1, 1.2))    # outer ring
)

# Back to Cartesian coordinates
lay_radial <- cbind(
  x = rho_scaled * cos(theta),
  y = rho_scaled * sin(theta)
)

# Optional: normalize again for plotting window
lay_radial <- apply(lay_radial, 2, scales::rescale, to = c(-1, 1))

node_xy <- nodes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    x = lay_radial[match(name, igraph::V(g)$name), 1],
    y = lay_radial[match(name, igraph::V(g)$name), 2],
    r = dplyr::if_else(type == "Term", term_pie_size, gene_pie_size)
  )





# Map each gene to the Terms it belongs to
gene_term_map <- df %>%
  dplyr::distinct(.data[[term_col]], .data[[gene_col]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data[[gene_col]]) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_terms = dplyr::n_distinct(.data[[term_col]]),
    sole_term = if (n_terms == 1) dplyr::first(.data[[term_col]]) else NA_character_,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join gene-term info onto node positions
node_xy <- node_xy %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_term_map, by = c("label" = gene_col))

# Term positions and a target point a bit inside the Term ring
term_xy <- node_xy %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "Term") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    term = label,
    tx = x,
    ty = y,
    tr = sqrt(x^2 + y^2)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # target radius for nearby unique-gene clusters
    target_r = tr * 0.82,
    ux = tx / tr,
    uy = ty / tr,
    target_x = ux * target_r,
    target_y = uy * target_r
  )

# Move each unique-gene cluster a little bit toward its sole Term,
# while keeping the cluster geometry intact
move_frac <- 0.40

for (tm in unique(gene_term_map$sole_term[!is.na(gene_term_map$sole_term)])) {
  idx <- which(
    node_xy$type == "Gene" &
      node_xy$n_terms == 1 &
      node_xy$sole_term == tm
  )

  if (length(idx) == 0) next

  trow <- term_xy[match(tm, term_xy$term), ]
  if (nrow(trow) == 0 || is.na(trow$term)) next

  # centroid of the unique-gene cluster
  cx <- mean(node_xy$x[idx], na.rm = TRUE)
  cy <- mean(node_xy$y[idx], na.rm = TRUE)

  # move the whole cluster partway toward the Term's target point
  dx <- (trow$target_x - cx) * move_frac
  dy <- (trow$target_y - cy) * move_frac

  node_xy$x[idx] <- node_xy$x[idx] + dx
  node_xy$y[idx] <- node_xy$y[idx] + dy
}

node_xy <- node_xy %>%
  dplyr::select(-n_terms, -sole_term)
  # Presence/absence of categories per node
  node_cats <- bind_rows(
    df %>% dplyr::transmute(name = paste0("T__", .data[[term_col]]),
                     broadCellCat = .data[[cat_col]]),
    df %>% dplyr::transmute(name = paste0("G__", .data[[gene_col]]),
                     broadCellCat = .data[[cat_col]])
  ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(present = 1) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = broadCellCat,
                values_from = present,
                values_fill = 0)
  
  ###### spread out the groups more
  gene_comp <- df %>%
  dplyr::distinct(.data[[gene_col]], .data[[term_col]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data[[gene_col]]) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_terms = dplyr::n_distinct(.data[[term_col]]),
    comp_key = paste(sort(unique(.data[[term_col]])), collapse = "||"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

node_xy <- node_xy %>%
  dplyr::left_join(gene_comp, by = c("label" = gene_col))

spread_factor <- 1.5   # increase to loosen more, e.g. 1.5
min_offset <- 0.01      # tiny floor so perfectly overlapping points separate

gene_groups <- unique(node_xy$comp_key[!is.na(node_xy$comp_key)])

for (ck in gene_groups) {
  idx <- which(node_xy$type == "Gene" & node_xy$comp_key == ck)

  if (length(idx) <= 1) next

  cx <- mean(node_xy$x[idx], na.rm = TRUE)
  cy <- mean(node_xy$y[idx], na.rm = TRUE)

  vx <- node_xy$x[idx] - cx
  vy <- node_xy$y[idx] - cy
  d  <- sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2)

  # If multiple points are identical, give them a tiny deterministic spread
  zero <- d < 1e-8
  if (any(zero)) {
    ang <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = sum(zero) + 1)[-(sum(zero) + 1)]
    vx[zero] <- cos(ang) * min_offset
    vy[zero] <- sin(ang) * min_offset
    d[zero]  <- sqrt(vx[zero]^2 + vy[zero]^2)
  }

  node_xy$x[idx] <- cx + vx * spread_factor
  node_xy$y[idx] <- cy + vy * spread_factor
}

node_xy <- node_xy %>%
  dplyr::select(-n_terms, -comp_key)

  # Make slices equal among present categories
  node_cats <- nodes %>%
    dplyr::select(name) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(node_cats, by = "name") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(all_of(cat_cols), ~replace_na(.x, 0)))

  rs <- rowSums(node_cats[cat_cols])
  node_cats[cat_cols] <- sweep(node_cats[cat_cols], 1, ifelse(rs == 0, 1, rs), "/")

  plot_nodes <- node_xy %>%
    dplyr::left_join(node_cats, by = "name") 

  edge_xy <- edges %>%
    dplyr::left_join(node_xy %>% dplyr::select(name, x, y), by = c("from" = "name")) %>%
    dplyr::rename(x1 = x, y1 = y) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(node_xy %>% dplyr::select(name, x, y), by = c("to" = "name")) %>%
    dplyr::rename(x2 = x, y2 = y)

  


 # pal <- setNames(scales::hue_pal()(length(cat_cols)), cat_cols)


pn <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_curve(
    data = edge_xy,
    aes(
      x = x1, y = y1,
      xend = x2, yend = y2,
      color = term
    ),
    curvature = 0.35,
    ncp = 10,
    linewidth = 1.2,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  scatterpie::geom_scatterpie(
    data = plot_nodes,
    aes(x = x, y = y, r = r),
    cols = cat_cols,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.25,
    alpha = 0.95
  ) +
  ggforce::geom_circle(
    data = dplyr::filter(plot_nodes, type == "Term"),
    aes(
      x0 = x,
      y0 = y,
      r = r,
      color = term
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 2,
    fill = NA
  ) +
  # Gene labels
ggplot2::geom_text(
  data = dplyr::filter(node_xy, type == "Gene"),
  aes(
    x = x,
    y = y,
    label = label
  ),
  size = size_gene_lab,
  vjust = vjust_gene_lab
) +

# Term labels
ggplot2::geom_text(
  data = dplyr::filter(node_xy, type == "Term"),
  aes(
    x = x * 1.50,
    y = y * 1.10,
    label = label
  ),
  size = size_term_lab,
  vjust = vjust_term_lab
)+
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = pal, drop = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = term_pal, guide = "none") +
ggplot2::coord_equal(clip = "off") +
  ggplot2::theme_void() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right")+
ggplot2::theme(
  plot.margin = grid::unit(c(2, 5, 2, 5), "lines")  # top, right, bottom, left
)
```

```{r collect_network_interferon_log2FC____save}

## ── helper: pattern → tissue & direction tag used in names_df ────────────────
network_configs <- list(
  list(pattern = "LN_up_upvsPRE",       tiss = "LN",   label = "upBOTH_LN"),
  list(pattern = "LN_notSig_upvsPRE",   tiss = "LN",   label = "upDAY8only_LN"),
  list(pattern = "LN_up_notSigvsPRE",   tiss = "LN",   label = "upDAY2only_LN"),
  list(pattern = "PBMC_up_upvsPRE",     tiss = "PBMC", label = "upBOTH_PBMC"),
  list(pattern = "PBMC_notSig_upvsPRE", tiss = "PBMC", label = "upDAY8only_PBMC"),
  list(pattern = "PBMC_up_notSigvsPRE", tiss = "PBMC", label = "upDAY2only_PBMC")
)

pathway_keywords_ifn <- c("Interferon", "interferon", "IFN")

all_network_log2fc <- data.frame()

for (cfg in network_configs) {

  ## 1. which cluster_tiss_dir tabs match this pattern?
  curr_tabs <- names_df$cluster_tiss_dir[
    grepl(cfg$pattern, names_df$cluster_tiss_dir)
  ]

  ## 2. pull enrichment rows for those tabs, filter to IFN terms, sig only
  curr_enrich_df <- data.frame()
  for (curr_tab in curr_tabs) {
    curr_enrich_df <- rbind(
      curr_enrich_df,
      list_of_enrichments[[curr_tab]] %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          cluster_tiss_dir = curr_tab,
          tissue  = str_before_first(str_after_first(curr_tab, "_"), "_"),
          cluster = str_before_first(curr_tab, "_")
        ) %>%
        dplyr::filter(Adjusted.P.value < 0.05)
    )
  }

  if (nrow(curr_enrich_df) == 0) next

  ## 3. keep IFN terms, collapse to meta-term, go long on genes
  ifn_genes <- curr_enrich_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(grepl(paste(pathway_keywords_ifn, collapse = "|"), Term)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      metaTerm = ifelse(
        grepl(paste(c("alpha", "beta", "type i "), collapse = "|"), tolower(Term)),
        "type I alpha/beta interferon",
        ifelse(
          grepl(paste(c("gamma", "type ii "), collapse = "|"), tolower(Term)),
          "type II gamma interferon",
          "interferon, type I/II not specified"
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    tidyr::separate_rows(Genes, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
    dplyr::select(gene = Genes, Term = metaTerm, cluster, tissue) %>%
    dplyr::distinct()

  genes_this_network <- unique(ifn_genes$gene)

  if (length(genes_this_network) == 0) next

  ## 4. pull per-animal log2FC from curr_degs_df_trim, compute ave across sig animals
log2fc_slice <- curr_degs_df_trim %>%
  dplyr::filter(gene %in% genes_this_network,
                Tissue  == cfg$tiss,
                cluster %in% str_before_first(curr_tabs, "_"))  %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      MB59_avg_log2FCSIG = ifelse(MB59_p_val_adj < 0.05, MB59_avg_log2FC, NA),
      MC90_avg_log2FCSIG = ifelse(MC90_p_val_adj < 0.05, MC90_avg_log2FC, NA),
      MC98_avg_log2FCSIG = ifelse(MC98_p_val_adj < 0.05, MC98_avg_log2FC, NA),
      MC73_avg_log2FCSIG = ifelse(MC73_p_val_adj < 0.05, MC73_avg_log2FC, NA),
      MF07_avg_log2FCSIG = ifelse(MF07_p_val_adj < 0.05, MF07_avg_log2FC, NA),
      MF30_avg_log2FCSIG = ifelse(MF30_p_val_adj < 0.05, MF30_avg_log2FC, NA)
    ) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ave_log2FC_sig_animals = mean(
        c(MB59_avg_log2FCSIG, MC90_avg_log2FCSIG, MC98_avg_log2FCSIG,
          MC73_avg_log2FCSIG, MF07_avg_log2FCSIG, MF30_avg_log2FCSIG),
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    ## attach which IFN meta-term(s) the gene appeared in for this network
    dplyr::left_join(
      ifn_genes %>%
        dplyr::group_by(gene) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(ifn_meta_terms = paste(sort(unique(Term)), collapse = " | "),
                         .groups = "drop"),
      by = "gene"
    ) %>%
    ## broad cell category
    dplyr::left_join(
      list_of_broadCats %>%
        tibble::enframe(name = "broadCellCat", value = "cluster") %>%
        tidyr::unnest(cluster),
      by = "cluster"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(network = cfg$label) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      network, gene, cluster, broadCellCat, Tissue, contrast,
      MB59_avg_log2FC, MC90_avg_log2FC, MC98_avg_log2FC,
      MC73_avg_log2FC, MF07_avg_log2FC, MF30_avg_log2FC,
      MB59_avg_log2FCSIG, MC90_avg_log2FCSIG, MC98_avg_log2FCSIG,
      MC73_avg_log2FCSIG, MF07_avg_log2FCSIG, MF30_avg_log2FCSIG,
      ave_log2FC_sig_animals, num_animals_sig, which_animals_sig,
      ifn_meta_terms
    )
  
  
  

  all_network_log2fc <- rbind(all_network_log2fc, log2fc_slice)
}
```

```{r broadcatUpset, results='asis'}
### NOTE: custom upset-style plot (bar chart of intersection sizes on top,
### dot-matrix of set membership in the middle, stacked cluster names at the
### bottom), sorted by (1) number of categories in the pattern (descending),
### then (2) which categories are present, using `level_order` as the
### tie-break key (matches the display order top-to-bottom in the dot
### matrix). Built manually rather than via ggupset::scale_x_upset() since
### that function only supports frequency-based sorting.
### `cat_colors` is a named vector (category label -> color) used for "member"
### dots; non-member dots are always grey regardless of cat_colors. If a
### category label isn't found in cat_colors (e.g. mixed-plot "(up)"/"(down)"
### suffixed labels), the suffix is stripped before lookup.
### Bars with <= gene_label_cutoff DEGs get their gene names stacked vertically
### above the "n = X" count label; bars with more just show the count.
### `cluster_list_col` (optional), if provided, is a list-column (same
### tidyeval style as list_col) giving each gene's contributing fine-grained
### cluster names (e.g. "ClusterA__up"); the UNION of unique clusters across
### all genes sharing a pattern is shown as a stacked text block underneath
### the dot-matrix panel for that pattern's column.
make_upset_plot <- function(df, list_col, level_order, cat_colors = NULL,
                            bar_color = "grey30",
                            gene_label_cutoff = 20, label_offset = 0.5,
                            cluster_list_col = NULL, title = "") {

  list_col <- rlang::enquo(list_col)
  cluster_list_col <- rlang::enquo(cluster_list_col)
  has_cluster_col <- !rlang::quo_is_null(cluster_list_col)

  ### one row per gene with its (already sorted-by-level_order) pattern key
  df_sorted <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      .cats = purrr::map(!!list_col, ~ .x[order(match(.x, rev(level_order)))]),
      .pattern_key = purrr::map_chr(.cats, ~ paste(.x, collapse = "|")),
      .n_cats = lengths(.cats)
    )

  if(has_cluster_col){
    df_sorted <- df_sorted %>%
      dplyr::mutate(.clusters = !!cluster_list_col)
  }

  ### intersection sizes per pattern, plus the actual gene names in each
  ### pattern (sorted alphabetically for a stable, readable stacked label),
  ### plus (if provided) the union of contributing cluster names per pattern
  group_summarise <- function(d){
    d %>%
      dplyr::group_by(.pattern_key, .n_cats) %>%
      {
        if(has_cluster_col){
          dplyr::summarise(.,
            n_genes = dplyr::n(),
            gene_list = paste(sort(gene), collapse = "\n"),
            cluster_list = paste(sort(unique(unlist(.clusters))), collapse = "\n"),
            .groups = "drop")
        }else{
          dplyr::summarise(.,
            n_genes = dplyr::n(),
            gene_list = paste(sort(gene), collapse = "\n"),
            .groups = "drop")
        }
      }
  }

 pattern_counts <- df_sorted %>%
    group_summarise() %>%
    ### sort: more categories first, then by which categories are present.
    ### NOTE: arrange() can't correctly compare list-columns element-by-element,
    ### so .sort_key is built as a single zero-padded string (e.g. "0103") from
    ### each category's position in level_order, which sorts correctly with a
    ### plain lexicographic arrange() -- this also fixes singleton ordering,
    ### which was previously scrambled because the list-column sort silently
    ### fell back to an unintended comparison
    dplyr::mutate(
      .sort_key = purrr::map_chr(
        stringr::str_split(.pattern_key, "\\|"),
        ~ paste(sprintf("%02d", match(.x, rev(level_order))), collapse = "")
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.n_cats), .sort_key) %>%
    ### build the bar label: always "n = X"; if <= cutoff, append the stacked
    ### gene names on subsequent lines. label_y adds a FIXED offset above the
    ### bar top (rather than using vjust, which scales the gap with text
    ### height/relative position and made taller stacks appear to float
    ### further from their bar than short ones)
    dplyr::mutate(
      bar_label = ifelse(n_genes <= gene_label_cutoff,
                         paste0("n = ", n_genes, "\n", gene_list),
                         paste0("n = ", n_genes)),
      label_y = n_genes + label_offset
    )

  pattern_levels <- pattern_counts$.pattern_key

  ### bar chart panel
  p_bar <- pattern_counts %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.pattern_key = factor(.pattern_key, levels = pattern_levels)) %>%
    ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = .pattern_key, y = n_genes)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = bar_color) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(y = label_y, label = bar_label), vjust = 0, hjust = 0.5,
                       size = 2.3, lineheight = 0.85) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.3))) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of DEGs", title = title) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                  axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank())

  ### dot-matrix panel: one row per category (in level_order), one column per pattern
  dot_df <- tidyr::expand_grid(.pattern_key = pattern_levels, category = level_order) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_member = purrr::map2_lgl(.pattern_key, category,
                                  ~ .y %in% stringr::str_split(.x, "\\|")[[1]]),
      .pattern_key = factor(.pattern_key, levels = pattern_levels),
      category = factor(category, levels = rev(level_order))
    )

  ### assign dot color: grey for non-members; for members, look up cat_colors
  ### by category label with any " (up)"/" (down)" suffix stripped first (for
  ### the mixed plot); fall back to grey10 if no color found for that category
  if(!is.null(cat_colors)){
    dot_df <- dot_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        .base_cat = str_remove_all(as.character(category), " \\((up|down)\\)$"),
        dot_color = dplyr::case_when(
          !is_member ~ "grey85",
          .base_cat %in% names(cat_colors) ~ cat_colors[.base_cat],
          TRUE ~ "grey10"
        )
      )
  }else{
    dot_df <- dot_df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(dot_color = ifelse(is_member, "grey10", "grey85"))
  }

  ### connecting lines between dots within each pattern
  line_df <- dot_df %>%
    dplyr::filter(is_member) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(.pattern_key) %>%
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() > 1) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(ymin = min(as.numeric(category)),
                     ymax = max(as.numeric(category)), .groups = "drop")

  p_dots <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = line_df,
                          ggplot2::aes(x = .pattern_key, xend = .pattern_key,
                                      y = ymin, yend = ymax),
                          color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = dot_df,
                        ggplot2::aes(x = .pattern_key, y = category,
                                    color = dot_color),
                        size = 2.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_identity() +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                  axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank())

  panels <- list(p_bar, p_dots)
  rel_heights <- c(2, 1)

  ### optional third panel: stacked cluster names per pattern, positioned
  ### directly under the dot-matrix column it corresponds to
  if(has_cluster_col){
    p_clusters <- pattern_counts %>%
      dplyr::mutate(.pattern_key = factor(.pattern_key, levels = pattern_levels)) %>%
      ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = .pattern_key, y = 1, label = cluster_list)) +
      ggplot2::geom_text(vjust = 1, hjust = 0.5, size = 2, lineheight = 0.85) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
      ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
      ggplot2::theme_void() +
      ggplot2::theme(plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 2, r = 5.5, b = 5.5, l = 5.5))

    panels <- c(panels, list(p_clusters))
    rel_heights <- c(rel_heights, 1.5)
  }

  cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = panels, ncol = 1, align = "v", axis = "lr",
                     rel_heights = rel_heights)
}

    ## =========================================================================
## ZOOM-IN PANELS for the 5 outlined bars (same broad-category combo, both
## up and down together):
##   - all 3 broad cats together (Bcell + CD4 + CD8)
##   - CD4 + CD8 together (excluding Bcell)
##   - Bcell alone
##   - CD4 alone
##   - CD8 alone
## For each: (A) one heatmap of log2FC per fine cluster with up genes and
## down genes both shown (split by a row annotation strip), (B) enrichment
## dot plot + table, done separately for the up set and down set.
##
## Drop this in right after the upset_up_df / upset_down_df / upset_mixed_df
## blocks, still INSIDE the curr_tiss / curr_contrast loop (so clust_per_gene,
## curr_df2, curr_tiss, curr_contrast, colors_vec, colors_df, outputEnrichr_dir,
## eval_run_enrichments, name_map, reverse_name_map, broadcols_to_use,
## finalnames_df are all in scope).
## =========================================================================

### ---- define the broad-category combos of interest (direction-agnostic;
### up and down genes for each combo are pulled together below) ----

zoom_defs <- list(
  "All3"   = c("Bcell","CD4","CD8"),
  "CD4CD8" = c("CD4","CD8"),
  "Bcell"  = c("Bcell"),
  "CD4"    = c("CD4"),
  "CD8"    = c("CD8")
)
    
    zoom_colors <- c("All3"="#FEBCFF",
                     "CD4CD8"="#FF7400",
                     "Bcell"="#8968CD",
                     "CD4"="#FFA500",
                     "CD8"="#EE0000")

### helper: genes whose BroadCats_up (or BroadCats_down) column is EXACTLY
### this set of categories -- i.e. "up in Bcell+CD4+CD8" means those 3 and
### only those 3 are up
get_geneset <- function(clust_per_gene_df, dir, cats){
  col_use <- if(dir == "up") "BroadCats_up" else "BroadCats_down"
  clust_per_gene_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.cats_here = strsplit(.data[[col_use]], ",")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(purrr::map_lgl(.cats_here, ~ setequal(.x[.x != ""], cats))) %>%
    dplyr::pull(gene) %>%
    unique()
}

### helper: run/read cached Enrichr results for one gene set + label
run_or_load_enrichment <- function(genes_vec, dataset_name){

  xlsx_path <- file.path(outputEnrichr_dir, paste0(dataset_name,"_Enrichr.output.xlsx"))

  if(length(genes_vec) < 3){
    return(NULL)
  }

  if(eval_run_enrichments == TRUE || !file.exists(xlsx_path)){

    genes_for_enrich <- data.frame(gene = genes_vec, comparison = dataset_name)

    write.table(genes_for_enrich, quote = FALSE, sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE,
               file = file.path(outputEnrichr_dir,"genes_zoom.txt"))

    enrichr.libraries <- c("GO_Biological_Process_2021","GO_Cellular_Component_2021",
                           "GO_Molecular_Function_2021","KEGG_2021_Human","MSigDB_Hallmark_2020",
                           "WikiPathway_2021_Human","Azimuth_Cell_Types_2021","Reactome_2021",
                           "Reactome_2016","BioPlanet_2019")

    doEnrichOneAtATime(DEG_table = genes_for_enrich, dataset = dataset_name, ngenes = NULL,
                       Enrichr_dir = outputEnrichr_dir, enrichr.libraries = enrichr.libraries,
                       minOverlap = 3, minAdjPval = 0.2)

    list_of_enrch <- readExcelTabs(xlsx_path)

  } else {

    list_of_enrch <- readExcelTabs(xlsx_path)

  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(list_of_enrch) %>%
    ### force numeric types, in case these were read back from Excel as
    ### character (e.g. if a column had mixed/odd formatting) -- bind_rows()
    ### across categories later will silently coerce everything to character
    ### if even one source data frame has these as character, which breaks
    ### any downstream log10()/sorting on Adjusted.P.value
    dplyr::mutate(
      P.value = as.numeric(P.value),
      Adjusted.P.value = as.numeric(Adjusted.P.value),
      Combined.Score = as.numeric(Combined.Score)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Adjusted.P.value < 0.05) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Adjusted.P.value)
}


### helper: print an enrichment dot plot + DT table for a given results df
print_enrichment_panel <- function(enrich_df, panel_title){

  if(is.null(enrich_df) || nrow(enrich_df) == 0){
    cat(" ",paste0("no enrichment terms with adjusted p < 0.05 (or too few genes to test)"),"\n")
    cat('\n')
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  cat(" ",paste0(nrow(enrich_df)," terms with adjusted p < 0.05"),"\n")
  cat('\n')

  top_n_terms <- 20

  plot_df <- enrich_df %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = top_n_terms) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      n_genes_overlap = stringr::str_count(Genes, ",") + 1,
      ### disambiguate Term labels first, since the same pathway Term can
      ### appear more than once (e.g. from different Gene.Set libraries, or
      ### multiple rows with the same Term/Gene.Set combo), which otherwise
      ### produces duplicate factor levels and errors out factor(Term, levels = rev(Term))
      Term_label = ifelse(
        duplicated(Term) | duplicated(Term, fromLast = TRUE),
        paste0(Term, " - ", Gene.Set),
        Term
      ),
      Term_label = make.unique(Term_label),
      Term_label = factor(Term_label, levels = rev(Term_label))
    )

  p_enrich <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df,
                              ggplot2::aes(x = -log10(Adjusted.P.value), y = Term_label,
                                          size = n_genes_overlap, color = Combined.Score)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::scale_color_gradient(low = "steelblue", high = "firebrick") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "-log10(adj. p-value)", y = NULL,
                  size = "Genes\noverlap", color = "Combined\nScore",
                  title = panel_title) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8))

  plot(p_enrich)

  cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n')

  to_print_enrich <- enrich_df %>%
    dplyr::relocate(Term) %>%
    DT::datatable(extensions = 'Buttons',
                  options = list(dom = 'Blfrtip',
                                 buttons = c('copy','csv','excel','pdf','print'),
                                 iDisplayLength = 25,
                                 lengthMenu = list(c(10,25,50,-1), c(10,25,50,"All")))) %>%
    formatSignif("P.value", 2) %>%
    formatSignif("Adjusted.P.value", 2) %>%
    formatRound("Combined.Score", 2)

  print(htmltools::tagList(to_print_enrich))
}

### Walk down the significance-ranked list of terms, clustering terms whose
### gene sets are highly similar (Jaccard similarity >= threshold) using
### single-linkage: a new term joins an existing cluster if it is similar
### enough to ANY term already in that cluster (not just the cluster's
### representative). The representative of each cluster is its most
### significant (first-encountered) term; all other member term names are
### folded into that representative's collapsed_terms, and the union of all
### member gene sets is reported in collapsed_genes. Stops once n distinct
### clusters have been collected (walking only as far into the ranked list
### as needed), so terms ranked after that point never get a chance to
### either form a new cluster or join an existing one.
collapse_redundant_gene_terms_topn <- function(df, n, jaccard_threshold = 0.5) {

  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(df)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Adjusted.P.value = as.numeric(Adjusted.P.value),
      Combined.Score = as.numeric(Combined.Score)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Adjusted.P.value, dplyr::desc(Combined.Score)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      .gene_set = purrr::map(
        stringr::str_split(Genes, ",\\s*"),
        ~ unique(.x)
      )
    )

  jaccard <- function(a, b) {
    inter <- length(intersect(a, b))
    uni <- length(union(a, b))
    if (uni == 0) return(0)
    inter / uni
  }

  ### each cluster: list(rep_idx = <row index of representative>,
  ###                    member_idx = <vector of all row indices in cluster>)
  clusters <- list()

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {

    gene_set_i <- df$.gene_set[[i]]

    ### find the best-matching existing cluster via single-linkage: max
    ### similarity to ANY member already in that cluster
    best_cluster <- NA_integer_
    best_sim <- 0

    if (length(clusters) > 0) {
      for (c_idx in seq_along(clusters)) {
        member_sims <- purrr::map_dbl(clusters[[c_idx]]$member_idx,
                                      ~ jaccard(gene_set_i, df$.gene_set[[.x]]))
        max_sim <- max(member_sims)
        if (max_sim > best_sim) {
          best_sim <- max_sim
          best_cluster <- c_idx
        }
      }
    }

    if (!is.na(best_cluster) && best_sim >= jaccard_threshold) {
      ### joins existing cluster -- does not consume a new slot
      clusters[[best_cluster]]$member_idx <- c(clusters[[best_cluster]]$member_idx, i)

    } else {
      ### no sufficiently similar existing cluster
      if (length(clusters) >= n) {
        ### already filled all n slots -- stop, since we only fill from the
        ### ranked order and this term doesn't join an existing cluster
        break
      }
      clusters[[length(clusters) + 1]] <- list(rep_idx = i, member_idx = i)
    }
  }

  rep_rows <- purrr::map_int(clusters, ~ .x$rep_idx)

  collapsed_terms_vec <- purrr::map_chr(clusters, function(cl) {
    paste(unique(df$Term[cl$member_idx]), collapse = "; ")
  })

  collapsed_genes_vec <- purrr::map_chr(clusters, function(cl) {
    all_genes <- unique(unlist(df$.gene_set[cl$member_idx]))
    paste(sort(all_genes), collapse = ", ")
  })

  df %>%
    dplyr::slice(rep_rows) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      collapsed_terms = collapsed_terms_vec,
      collapsed_genes = collapsed_genes_vec
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-.gene_set)
}

### Build the deduplicated, top-n-per-category combined enrichment table,
### with all the annotation columns needed for plotting (n_collapsed,
### Term_label, display_label, etc.) but no plotting side effects. Returns
### NULL if there's nothing to show.
build_combined_enrichment_df <- function(enrich_by_cat_list, top_n = 10, jaccard_threshold = 0.6) {

  combined_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(enrich_by_cat_list, function(df, cat_name) {
    if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)
    df %>%
      collapse_redundant_gene_terms_topn(n = top_n, jaccard_threshold = jaccard_threshold) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(zoom_cat = cat_name)
  })

  if (nrow(combined_df) == 0) return(NULL)

  combined_df <- combined_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      n_genes_overlap = stringr::str_count(Genes, ",") + 1,
      ### count how many original terms were folded into this row
      n_collapsed = stringr::str_count(collapsed_terms, "; ") + 1,
      Term_label = ifelse(
        duplicated(paste(Term, zoom_cat)) | duplicated(paste(Term, zoom_cat), fromLast = TRUE),
        paste0(Term, " - ", Gene.Set),
        Term
      ),
      Term_label = make.unique(Term_label),
      zoom_cat = factor(zoom_cat, levels = names(enrich_by_cat_list))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(zoom_cat, Adjusted.P.value) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Term_label = factor(Term_label, levels = rev(unique(Term_label))))

  ### display label: append "(n)" if more than one term was collapsed into
  ### this row, plain term name otherwise
  combined_df <- combined_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      display_label = ifelse(
        n_collapsed > 1,
        paste0(Term, " (", n_collapsed, ")"),
        as.character(Term)
      )
    )

  combined_df
}

### Plot + print table for an already-built combined enrichment df (see
### build_combined_enrichment_df()). Keeping this separate from the data-build
### step lets callers compute shared axis limits across multiple calls (e.g.
### up vs down) before any plotting happens.
print_combined_enrichment_panel <- function(combined_df, panel_title, x_max = NULL) {

  if (is.null(combined_df) || nrow(combined_df) == 0) {
    cat(" ", paste0("no enrichment terms with adjusted p < 0.05 for any category"), "\n")
    cat('\n')
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  ### named vector keyed by factor level, for scale_y_discrete(labels = ...)
  label_lookup <- combined_df %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Term_label, display_label)
  label_vec <- setNames(label_lookup$display_label, label_lookup$Term_label)

  x_limits <- if (!is.null(x_max)) c(0, x_max) else NULL

p_enrich <- ggplot2::ggplot(combined_df,
                              ggplot2::aes(x = -log10(Adjusted.P.value), y = Term_label,
                                          size = n_genes_overlap, color = zoom_cat)) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = label_vec) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = zoom_colors)+
    ggplot2::labs(x = "-log10(adj. p-value)", y = NULL,
                  size = "Genes\noverlap", color = "Zoom\ncategory",
                  title = panel_title) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7))

  if (!is.null(x_limits)) {
    p_enrich <- p_enrich + ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = x_limits)
  }

  plot(p_enrich)

  cat("\n")
  cat(' \n \n')

   list_of_plotted[[panel_title]] <<- combined_df %>% ### needs double << to write to the list from within the function
  dplyr::rename(Term_genes=Genes) %>%
    dplyr::relocate(zoom_cat, Term, collapsed_terms, Term_genes, collapsed_genes)

          " | n clusters_in_scope=", length(clusters_in_scope))

  heat_df <- curr_df2 %>%
    dplyr::filter(gene %in% zoom_genes_all, cluster %in% clusters_in_scope) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, cluster, avg_log2FC) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(gene, cluster) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(avg_log2FC = mean(avg_log2FC, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = cluster, values_from = avg_log2FC) %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("gene")

  ### drop clusters with no data for this gene set, and genes with no data
  ### across all remaining clusters
  heat_df <- heat_df[, colSums(!is.na(heat_df)) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  heat_df <- heat_df[rowSums(!is.na(heat_df)) > 0, , drop = FALSE]

  if(nrow(heat_df) < 1 || ncol(heat_df) < 1){

    cat(" ",paste0("not enough data to plot a heatmap for this set"),"\n")
    cat('\n')

  } else {

    ### no clustering: columns follow the fixed clusters_order used
    ### throughout the report; rows are grouped by direction (up block on
    ### top, down block below), and within each block sorted by mean log2FC
    ### so the strongest genes are nearest the direction boundary
    col_order_fixed <- intersect(colors_df$cluster, colnames(heat_df))
    heat_df <- heat_df[, col_order_fixed, drop = FALSE]

    row_mean_fc <- rowMeans(heat_df, na.rm = TRUE)

    direction_vec <- ifelse(rownames(heat_df) %in% up_genes, "up", "down")

    row_order_final <- c(
      rownames(heat_df)[direction_vec == "up"][order(-row_mean_fc[direction_vec == "up"])],
      rownames(heat_df)[direction_vec == "down"][order(row_mean_fc[direction_vec == "down"])]
    )

    heat_df <- heat_df[row_order_final, , drop = FALSE]
    direction_vec <- direction_vec[match(row_order_final, names(direction_vec)[order(match(names(direction_vec), row_order_final))])]

    direction_vec <- ifelse(rownames(heat_df) %in% up_genes, "up", "down")

                     scale_range_zoom)

    ### gap between the up block and down block (row-wise)
    n_up_present <- sum(direction_vec == "up")
    gaps_row_use <- if(n_up_present > 0 && n_up_present < nrow(heat_df)) n_up_present else NULL

    # )
    # print(p_heat)
  }

  cat("\n")

  )
  enrich_down_by_cat[[curr_zoom]] <- run_or_load_enrichment(
    down_genes,
    paste0("z",curr_tiss,contrast_short[curr_contrast],curr_zoom,"dn")
  )

  

}

     cat("### ",paste0(fig_name_to_use,"b - up only"),"\n")
```

```{r setFig_acuteISG}
                     dplyr::distinct(),
                   by = "source") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source_final = source) %>%
    ### get average of avg_log2FC across cell subsets
  dplyr::select(source_final,ligand) %>%
  unique() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ligand) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(numCelltypes = n()) %>%
```
